name: Queen of Sheba
bio: The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame and came to Jerusalem with a very great caravan — camels laden with spices, gold, and precious stones — to test him with hard questions. Solomon answered everything she asked; nothing was too difficult for him to explain. When she saw his wisdom, the palace he had built, the food on his table, the seating of his officials, the attendance of his servants, their attire, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he made at the temple, she was overwhelmed. She told the king that the report she had heard in her own land had not come close to the reality: "Not even half was told me; your wisdom and wealth far exceed the report I heard. How happy your people must be! How happy your officials, who continually stand before you and hear your wisdom! Praise be to the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and placed you on the throne of Israel" (1 Kings 10:1-9). She gave Solomon 120 talents of gold, along with a great quantity of spices and precious stones — more spices than were ever brought to Israel again — and Solomon gave her, out of his royal bounty, all she desired, beyond what he gave her in exchange for her own gifts; she then returned with her retinue to her own country (1 Kings 10:10, 13).
